supporting_evidence.description: Alleged History: Road Traffic Accident at Shankar Road T-Point at approximately 18:20 hours.
Patient riding scooter, hit by speeding motorcycle from side. Thrown off vehicle and landed on road.
Helmet worn at time of accident.
Brought Dead: False
Condition On Arrival: Conscious but disoriented, GCS 13/15 (E3 V4 M6), in severe pain, bleeding from scalp wound
Blood Pressure: 100/70 mmHg
Pulse: 112/min
Respiratory Rate: 24/min
Temperature: 98.4°F
Spo2: 94% on room air
Pain Score: 9/10

Item 1: Injury Id: INJ-001, Type: Laceration, Location: Scalp, right parietal region, Size: 6cm x 2cm x 1cm deep, Description: Irregular wound with active bleeding, visible periosteum, no skull bone visible, Cause: Impact with road surface

Item 2: Injury Id: INJ-002, Type: Abrasion, Location: Face, right cheek and forehead, Size: Multiple, covering 12cm x 8cm area, Description: Road rash, dirt and debris embedded in wounds, Cause: Sliding on road surface

Item 3: Injury Id: INJ-003, Type: Closed fracture, Location: Right femur, mid-shaft, Description: Deformity of right thigh, swelling, abnormal mobility, crepitus present. X-ray confirmed comminuted fracture mid-shaft femur with displacement., Cause: Direct impact from vehicle collision

Item 4: Injury Id: INJ-004, Type: Fracture, Location: Right clavicle, middle third, Description: Tenderness and deformity over right clavicle. X-ray confirmed displaced fracture., Cause: Fall on right shoulder

Item 5: Injury Id: INJ-005, Type: Fractures, Location: Ribs 3rd, 4th, 5th on right side, anterior, Description: Chest X-ray shows fractures of right 3rd, 4th, 5th ribs anteriorly. No flail segment. Lung fields clear., Cause: Impact trauma
Item 6: Injury Id: INJ-006, Type: Abrasion, Location: Right forearm and elbow, Size: 15cm x 6cm, Description: Deep abrasion, oozing, Cause: Road contact
Item 7: Injury Id: INJ-007, Type: Abrasion, Location: Left knee, Size: 5cm x 4cm, Description: Superficial abrasion, Cause: Road contact
Test: X-Ray Skull AP and Lateral - Finding: No skull fracture. Normal study.
Test: X-Ray Right Femur AP and Lateral - Finding: Comminuted fracture mid-shaft right femur. 2.5cm shortening. Angulation present.
Test: X-Ray Right Clavicle - Finding: Displaced fracture middle third right clavicle.
Test: X-Ray Chest PA - Finding: Fracture right 3rd, 4th, 5th ribs anteriorly. No pneumothorax or hemothorax. Lung fields clear.
Test: CT Scan Head (Plain) - Finding: Small subdural hematoma right fronto-parietal region (8mm thickness, 3cm x 4cm). Midline shift 4mm to left. No mass effect. Basal cisterns patent.
Test: FAST Ultrasound Abdomen - Finding: Grade II liver laceration right lobe (3cm x 2cm). No free fluid in Morrison's pouch, splenorenal recess, or pelvis. Other organs normal.
Hemoglobin: 10.2 gm/dL
Tlc: 12000/cumm
Platelets: 2.4 lakhs/cumm
Blood Sugar: 130 mg/dL (Random)
Blood Urea: 32 mg/dL
Serum Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
Liver Function: Normal
Hiv Hbsag Hcv: Negative
Blood Alcohol Level: Nil (0 mg/dL)
Toxicology Screen: Negative for common drugs of abuse
Speedometer: Needle stuck at 55 kmph (indicates approximate speed at impact)
Headlight: Smashed, filament examination shows 'hot shock' deformation confirming light was ON at time of impact
Front Wheel: Rim bent, tyre burst on right side
Brake System: Front disc brake functional, rear drum brake functional. Brake lever in applied position consistent with emergency braking
Impact Force Calculated: Approximately 18-22 kN based on deformation pattern
Paint Evidence: White paint transfer on right front fork matching Activa body color
Right Side Impact: Deformation depth 25cm on right body panel indicating lateral impact force
Paint Evidence: Red paint transfer on right side panel matching Pulsar color
Brake Lever: Right brake lever bent due to impact, position suggests braking attempt
Tyres: Both tyres in good condition, adequate tread depth (3.5mm front, 4.0mm rear)

Conclusion: Primary impact was between front-right portion of Pulsar and right-center portion of Activa at an angle of 70-80 degrees. Pulsar was traveling at minimum 50-55 kmph at moment of impact. Both vehicle brake systems were functional prior to accident. Impact force sufficient to cause grievous injuries to rider of Activa.
Outer Shell: Multiple impact marks on right temporal and parietal region. Deep gouge 4cm long on right side
Inner Liner: Compressed on right side indicating absorption of impact energy
Chin Strap: Intact and fastened at time of impact (tear pattern confirms)
Blood: Blood stains inside helmet, Group B+ confirmed
Hair: Scalp hair fragments with root, suitable for DNA
Cracks: Two linear cracks on outer shell right side, 8cm and 5cm, indicating impact absorption
Effectiveness: Helmet prevented direct skull fracture. Damage pattern consistent with head impact on road surface
Outer Shell: Minor scratches on left side
Inner Liner: Normal, no compression
Chin Strap: Found torn - examination reveals it was already torn/damaged before accident, not due to accident forces
Conclusion: Helmet not properly secured at time of accident. Scratches consistent with minor fall.
Blood Group: B+
Alcohol: Not detected (0 mg/dL)
Drugs Toxicology: Negative for all screened substances
Dna Profile: Extracted and preserved for identification
Blood Group: O+
Pre Impact Scenario: Pulsar traveling SW to NE on Shankar Road towards junction. Activa traveling from Rajinder Nagar side and executing right turn towards Old Rajinder Nagar.
Impact Configuration: Pulsar front collides with right center of Activa at intersection. Impact angle 75 degrees.
Post Impact Dynamics: Activa rider thrown to right side, landing 4.2m from impact point. Pulsar falls to right side, slides 3.1m. Pulsar rider falls to left, minimal travel distance.

Speed At Impact: Pulsar: 52-58 kmph (calculated from skid mark length 4.2m, friction coefficient 0.7 for dry bitumen, and residual impact velocity from damage analysis). Activa: 8-12 kmph (typical turning speed).

Avoidability: At speed of 40 kmph (legal limit), Pulsar could have stopped in 15.5m total (thinking + braking distance). From skid mark evidence, Pulsar was at least 8m from impact point when emergency braking initiated. At legal speed, collision was avoidable. At actual speed (55 kmph), stopping distance required was 25m, making collision unavoidable from point where braking started.
Violation: Speed exceeding legal limit was the primary causative factor. Signal violation/secondary as signal was non-functional but traffic police manual direction was ignored.
18:20:03 - White Activa enters frame from bottom (Rajinder Nagar side), speed low, indicator blinking for right turn
18:20:05 - Red Pulsar enters frame from left (Shankar Road, Karol Bagh side), speed visibly high
18:20:06 - Traffic constable visible at junction, left hand raised signaling STOP for Shankar Road traffic
18:20:07 - Pulsar does not stop, continues at same speed into junction
18:20:07.5 - Pulsar front collides with right side of Activa
18:20:08 - Activa rider airborne, falls near road edge
18:20:09 - Pulsar rider falls, gets up at 18:20:12
18:20:14 - Constable runs towards Pulsar rider
18:20:18 - Constable grabs Pulsar rider by arm
Time stamp verified: Camera clock accurate within 2 seconds of IST
18:19:45 - Red Pulsar passes ATM at high speed, rider wearing red t-shirt, delivery bag visible
18:19:52 - Pulsar continues towards junction (towards St. Stephen's Hospital), brake light not visible at any point
18:20:30 - Several people seen running towards junction
Conclusion: CCTV footage corroborates witness statements. Confirms overspeeding, disregard of traffic police signal, and sequence of collision. Time stamps consistent with timeline.

On 15-10-2024 at about 18:20 hours, accused Amit Verma while riding motorcycle Bajaj Pulsar DL2SBP1234 on Shankar Road in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life, coming from Karol Bagh side towards Rajinder Nagar, at T-point near St. Stephen's Hospital Gate No. 2, jumped the red light and dashed against Honda Activa DL5SCT5678 being ridden by victim Rajesh Kumar Sharma who was coming from Rajinder Nagar side and taking a legal turn towards Old Rajinder Nagar. Due to high-speed impact, victim sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to St. Stephen's Hospital in critical condition. The accused failed to provide medical aid to victim and attempted to flee but was apprehended by Traffic Constable Mohammed Asif at the spot. Medical examination of accused was conducted and case has been registered.

Received DD No. 24-A dated 15-10-2024 regarding accident at Shankar Road T-Point at 18:20 hours. Proceeded to spot. PCR already present. Victim shifted to St. Stephen's Hospital. Accused detained at spot by Traffic Constable Mohammed Asif. Conducted preliminary inquiry at spot. Collected initial evidence. Registered FIR No. 452/2024 under sections 281/125 BNS and 184/134 MV Act on complaint of Smt. Sunita Sharma, wife of victim. Arrested accused Amit Verma at 19:15 hours from spot. Conducted personal search, prepared arrest memo. Accused sent for medical examination to RML Hospital through Constable Rajesh. Victim's MLC obtained from St. Stephen's Hospital - grievous injuries noted. IO to hospital, recorded victim's medical status. Returned to spot for detailed panchnama.
Exhibits Collected: Vehicle DL2SBP1234, DL5SCT5678, accused's mobile, both DLs, helmets
Statements Recorded: Complaint of Sunita Sharma, Statement of HC Mohammed Asif (eyewitness), Statement of Prakash Joshi (eyewitness)

Conducted detailed spot panchnama at Shankar Road T-Point from 21:00 to 22:15 hours in presence of panch witnesses Mohammed Asif and Prakash Joshi. Took measurements of road width (12.5m Shankar Road, 10m Rajinder Nagar Road), vehicle positions, skid marks (4.2m from Pulsar), blood stains, debris field. Identified impact point 6.5m from Shankar Road stop line. Photographed scene - 25 digital frames by HC Ramesh Kumar. Collected broken vehicle parts, helmets, delivery bag. Arranged for both vehicles to be towed to PS Malkhana yard. Noted non-functional traffic signal, 4 of 6 street lights working. Panchnama completed at 22:15 hours.
Exhibits Collected: Broken parts, helmets, delivery bag, blood samples (through hospital)
Photographs: 25 digital frames

Accused Amit Verma produced before me in lock-up. Informed him of his rights under Article 20(3) of Constitution and right to legal counsel. Accused opted to give voluntary statement without lawyer. Recorded detailed statement of accused in presence of ASI Ramphal Singh as witness. Accused admitted overspeeding and stated he was in hurry to deliver Zomato order. Showed remorse. Statement recorded verbatim. Accused remanded to judicial custody. Duty Magistrate informed telephonically. Accused to be produced before Ld. MM tomorrow.
Statements Recorded: Accused statement of Amit Verma

Morning: Directed ASI Rajender Prasad (MTO) to conduct detailed mechanical inspection of both vehicles. Inspection conducted 10:00-13:30 in Malkhana yard. Report received - both vehicles roadworthy before accident, damage consistent with collision dynamics, Pulsar speedometer stuck at 55 kmph. Mid-day: Visited St. Stephen's Hospital security office. Collected CCTV DVR hard disk from Gate 2 camera (CAM-SSH-G2-03) covering junction. Obtained footage from 18:00-18:45 hours. Chain of custody documented. Also visited Canara Bank ATM, Shankar Road. Bank Manager Mr. S. Venkatesh provided CCTV copy on pen drive showing approach road. Obtained PCR Van Z-45 dashcam SD card from ASI Dharampal. All digital evidence submitted to HC Ramesh Kumar, Technical Cell for analysis.
Exhibits Collected: CCTV DVR (EVD-0452-013), CCTV Pen Drive (EVD-0452-014), PCR Dashcam SD (EVD-0452-015)
Reports Received: Vehicle Inspection Report from ASI Rajender Prasad

Visited St. Stephen's Hospital SICU. Met treating doctor Dr. Anjali Mehta. Victim Rajesh Sharma still in ICU, post-surgery for femur fracture. Also underwent craniotomy for SDH evacuation on 16-10-2024 morning. Condition critical but stable. Doctor confirmed injuries are grievous in nature and dangerous to life. Obtained detailed MLC and medical records. Collected victim's blood sample for FSL (alcohol/drug screening - negative as per hospital). Met complainant Sunita Sharma at hospital, briefed her on investigation progress. Advised her to preserve all medical bills and records for court.
Documents Obtained: MLC Report, Admission records, Surgery notes

HC Ramesh Kumar completed CCTV footage analysis. Report confirms: Pulsar overspeeding (60 kmph on approach, 52-58 at impact), ignored traffic constable's stop signal, collision at 18:20:07.800 hours. Activa at normal turning speed (10 kmph), legal turn. Footage from 3 cameras synchronized and consistent. Prepared detailed CCTV analysis report with frame-by-frame speed calculation. All exhibits packed and sealed for FSL examination: vehicles, helmets, broken parts, blood samples, photographs SD card, CCTV HDD. Dispatched to FSL Rohini through Constable Mohan Singh with Road Certificate No. 234/2024 dated 17-10-2024. FSL requisition letter prepared detailing examination required.
Reports Received: CCTV Analysis Report
Exhibits Sent Fsl: EVD-0452-001, 002, 006, 007, 008, 010, 011, 012, 013

Produced accused Amit Verma before Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate, Tis Hazari Courts. Filed application for 3-day police custody remand for further investigation - need to recover Zomato delivery records, verify accused's mobile data, and conduct test identification parade. Court granted 2 days PC remand. Accused remanded to police custody till 20-10-2024. Also filed application for preservation of CCTV footage from other cameras on route. Court directed concerned authorities to preserve footage for 30 days.
Court Orders: PC Remand for 2 days, CCTV preservation order

During PC remand, extracted data from accused's smartphone (Samsung M32) with technical assistance from IT Cell. Recovered: Zomato Partner App data showing order accepted at 18:10, pickup from Haldiram's Karol Bagh at 18:15, delivery address in Old Rajinder Nagar with deadline 18:35. GPS location history shows speeds of 55-65 kmph on Shankar Road segment. Also recovered Google Maps timeline confirming route and speeds. Obtained Zomato records through official communication to Zomato's nodal officer - confirmation of accused's delivery partner ID, order details, and delivery attempt at 18:35 which was marked 'delayed'. Mobile call log shows no calls at time of accident - accused not distracted by phone call, but was possibly looking at navigation. Phone mounted on handlebar confirmed.
Digital Evidence: Zomato Partner App data, Google Maps Timeline, GPS speed logs

Test Identification Parade not conducted as accused identified by witnesses at spot itself. Section 164 CrPC statement of witnesses not deemed necessary. Accused produced before Ld. MM on expiry of PC remand. Accused not applying for bail at this stage. Court sent accused to judicial custody. Investigation continued. Visited traffic police circle office, obtained record of complaint filed by Constable Asif about non-functional signal on 13-10-2024. Also obtained duty roster confirming Asif's deployment at Shankar Road T-Point on 15-10-2024 from 16:00-20:00 hours.
Documents Obtained: Traffic signal complaint record, Duty roster

Visited St. Stephen's Hospital. Victim shifted from ICU to general ward on 24-10-2024. Conscious and oriented. Recorded supplementary statement of victim under Section 161 CrPC. Victim states he was returning home from office, wearing helmet, driving at 30-35 kmph, took right turn at T-point when suddenly a speeding motorcycle hit him. He does not remember anything after that. Victim's statement corroborates evidence. Doctor indicates another 2 weeks hospitalization needed. Physiotherapy to follow. Permanent disability not ruled out for right leg.
Statements Recorded: Supplementary statement of victim Rajesh Sharma

Background verification of accused conducted through local inquiry at Old Rajinder Nagar address and native village in Moradabad, UP through UP Police. Accused has no previous criminal record. Living in Delhi for 5 years. Working with Zomato for 2 years. Two-wheeler driving experience 7 years. No previous traffic challans in Delhi (verified from e-challan portal). However, one challan for overspeeding in Moradabad in 2022 (paid). Landlord confirms accused is of good character. No history of rashness or alcoholism. Accused's father is a marginal farmer. Family background verified.
Documents Obtained: Background verification report, E-challan portal screenshot

Received preliminary FSL report from Dr. Priya Nambiar. Key findings: Speed at impact 52-58 kmph for Pulsar, victim's helmet prevented skull fracture but sustained significant impact, blood alcohol negative for both, vehicle damage consistent with collision dynamics, paint transfer confirmed. Accident reconstruction confirms primary fault of Pulsar rider. Formal report awaited. Preliminary findings included in case file for reference.
Reports Received: Preliminary FSL findings (verbal and email)

Received final FSL Report No. FSL/DL/2024/PHY/8934 dated 18-11-2024. Complete forensic examination confirms all investigation findings. Report includes vehicle examination, helmet analysis, blood analysis, accident reconstruction, and CCTV correlation. All exhibits returned from FSL to Malkhana. FSL report made part of case file. Key conclusions: (1) Accident caused by overspeeding of Pulsar (52-58 kmph vs 40 kmph limit), (2) Victim had no contributory negligence, (3) Helmet saved victim from fatal head injury, (4) Both vehicles mechanically sound before accident.
Reports Received: FSL Report No. FSL/DL/2024/PHY/8934

Victim Rajesh Sharma discharged from hospital on 20-11-2024 after 36 days of treatment. Obtained final discharge summary and fitness certificate. Victim advised 3 months physiotherapy, follow-up in Ortho and Neuro OPD. Permanent disability assessment after 6 months. Recorded final statement of victim regarding expenses incurred (approximately ■4.2 lakhs medical expenses), loss of salary (3 months leave without pay), and ongoing treatment needs. Victim expresses desire for compensation and strict punishment to accused. Documents collected for Victim Compensation Scheme application.
Statements Recorded: Final victim statement
Documents Obtained: Discharge summary, Medical bills, Salary slips, Physiotherapy prescription

Investigation complete. All evidence collected, statements recorded, forensic reports received. Prima facie case well established against accused Amit Verma for offences under Section 281 BNS (Rash driving), Section 125 BNS (Act endangering life), Section 184 MV Act (Dangerous driving), and Section 134 MV Act (Failure to provide medical aid - accused did not actively assist victim though he was also injured, however the attempt to leave initially constitutes violation). Evidence list finalized - 15 exhibits. Case diary complete with 15 entries. All documents compiled and indexed in Annexures. Investigation reveals: Accused was overspeeding (52-58 kmph in 40 kmph zone), ignored traffic constable's manual stop signal, was in hurry to meet food delivery deadline, and due to high speed could not stop in time to avoid collision with victim's scooter who was making a legal turn at appropriate speed. Victim suffered grievous injuries requiring 36 days hospitalization and may have permanent disability. No contributory negligence by victim. Accused has no criminal history but his actions show disregard for traffic rules and public safety. Prepared final investigation report recommending filing of chargesheet before Hon'ble Court under above sections. Report submitted to ACP, Patel Nagar Sub-Division for supervisory review and approval.
Reports Prepared: Investigation Completion Report, Draft Chargesheet
Submitted To: ACP Patel Nagar for approval
